source_text: In the United States, a 2024 systematic review of neonatal male circumcision reaffirmed public health benefits such as reduced urinary tract infections and sexually transmitted infections, countering ethical critiques but noting no formal policy update from the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) since its 2012 statement, which was informally reaffirmed amid declining rates from 58.3% in 2012 to lower figures by 2022 per Johns Hopkins data. [207]
